headline: ASX slipped slightly today as rate-cut hopes evaporate — economists now say no relief until 2027, while gold surges to record highs and your US holdings had a solid session last night.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 1.72% today, giving back some of last week's gains. Despite some talk of a lithium recovery, the sector remains under pressure as lithium prices stay subdued globally. With no rate cuts on the horizon until 2027, the cost environment for miners remains tough and speculative names like PLS get hit hardest.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a solid session last night, up 1.87% to $254.99. No specific news catalyst was obvious, but the stock has been benefiting from broader optimism around the gaming sector and anticipation of upcoming title releases. Overall up 11.2% on your cost basis — a nice win so far.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft bounced 1.62% last night to $390.49, continuing its recovery. The market is rewarding Microsoft's strong AI positioning — its Copilot and Azure AI products are seen as a key growth driver. Note the stock is still down ~11.9% on your total investment, so this is a bounce in a hole, not a new high.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL gained 1.3% today, which is a bit of a surprise given crude oil fell 1.06% last night to $67.96/barrel. The ETF likely got a lift from energy sector rotation on the ASX and a rising AUD, which can sometimes boost hedged international energy holdings. Oil's slide on softer demand signals is worth watching for this one.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.6% today to $95.67. A rising AUD (up 0.27% to 69.34 US cents) can be a slight headwind for unhedged international ETFs, but emerging markets had a decent session, likely helped by firmer sentiment in Asian markets.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI barely moved today, up just 0.12% to $16.76. The AI theme remains in focus globally but the NASDAQ was soft last night (down 0.8%), which tends to weigh on AI-focused ETFs the following ASX session. Still down 11.3% on your cost — patience required here.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, up just 0.09% to $76.28. As a diversified fund holding global and Aussie shares, it tends to move slowly — that's the point. FY26 was reportedly a strong year for Vanguard's global ETF range, with VGS leading gains, and VDHG would have benefited from that tailwind.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was dead flat today at $533.31, reflecting that the S&P 500 barely moved last night (essentially unchanged at 7,483). The US market is pausing after recent gains — nothing alarming, just a breather.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.48% last night to $356.18. No major news catalyst — this looks like the market rotating slightly toward Microsoft's AI story over Google's. GOOG is still up 15.9% on your cost basis, so this is a minor wobble in a healthy position.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium still struggling
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell 1.72% today to $5.14 and is now down nearly 24% on your investment. The lithium recovery narrative is circulating, but there's no hard price catalyst yet. With rate cuts pushed to 2027, the broader risk-off mood doesn't help speculative miners. Hold for now unless you want to cut losses — but this one needs a real lithium price move to recover.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Recovery underway but still underwater
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 1.62% last night to $390.49, but you're still down ~$48 AUD on this position. The TradingView note flagging 'record earnings but -30% from highs' is worth keeping in mind — the fundamentals are strong (AI/Azure growth) but the entry price is working against you. Hold and let the AI tailwind do its job over time.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF barely moving despite global AI buzz
watch_today.detail: GXAI crept up just 0.12% today and remains 11.3% below your cost. The AI theme is everywhere in the news — model leaks, regulation debates, new product launches — but the ETF hasn't caught fire yet. NASDAQ weakness last night (down 0.8%) is a drag. Worth holding given the long-term AI trend, but don't expect a quick recovery.

watch_today.title: No RBA rate cuts until 2027 — Australia worst for inflation
watch_today.detail: Multiple economists are now ruling out any Reserve Bank rate cuts until 2027, and one is even flagging a possible fourth rate rise. Australia has topped inflation rankings among all major developed economies — meaning your mortgage or any debt is staying expensive longer. This is a headwind for the ASX broadly and could weigh on growth stocks. Something to factor into your planning.

watch_today.title: Gold surging — good tailwind for diversified holdings
watch_today.detail: Gold hit $4,172/oz last night, up 1.46% in a single session — that's a big single-day move. Gold's rise usually signals investors are nervous about something (inflation, geopolitical risk, or currency weakness). If you hold any gold-exposed assets or are thinking about adding a safe-haven position, now's a relevant moment to consider it.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Gaming stock on a roll
watch_today.detail: Take-Two Interactive is up 1.87% last night and 11.2% above your cost basis. No specific news, but the stock is building momentum. Consider whether you want to let this run further or lock in some gains — there's no urgent reason to sell, but it's the standout winner in your portfolio right now.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 dipped slightly today, closing down 0.15% at 8,831 — nothing dramatic, just a quiet Monday session weighed down by the grim news that rate cuts won't arrive until 2027 at the earliest. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 was essentially unchanged (flat as a pancake at 7,483), but the NASDAQ slid 0.8% as tech stocks took a breather. The big story was gold, which surged 1.46% to $4,173/oz — a big single-session move suggesting investors are nervous about inflation and geopolitics. Oil fell 1.06% to $67.96/barrel on softer demand signals. The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly to 69.34 US cents.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is interest rates — economists are now united in saying no Reserve Bank cuts until 2027, with Australia sitting at the top of developed-world inflation rankings. Not exactly cheery reading for anyone with a mortgage or business loan.

stories.title: No rate cuts until 2027 — and a fourth rise is possible, economists warn
stories.why_it_matters: Leading economists have effectively ruled out any Reserve Bank of Australia interest rate cuts until 2027, with at least one forecaster flagging the possibility of a fourth consecutive rate rise. The trigger is Australia's inflation problem — we're now ranked the worst among all major developed economies for inflation. That means mortgage repayments, business borrowing costs, and consumer spending pressure all stay elevated for longer. For investors, this is a signal that the ASX may stay under pressure, especially rate-sensitive sectors like property and retail.

stories.title: Australia tops inflation rankings among all major developed economies
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's inflation rate is now the highest among all major developed economies — worse than the US, UK, Europe, and Canada. This is particularly striking given the RBA has already lifted rates multiple times. It puts enormous pressure on the central bank to keep rates high or even raise them again. For everyday Aussies, it means the cost of living squeeze isn't going away anytime soon, and the government will face more political heat heading toward the next election cycle.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by the global conversation around regulation — with the UN, Europe, Spain, and the US all taking very different approaches to reining in (or not) artificial intelligence. There are also some juicy model leaks floating around if you're into that sort of thing.

stories.title: UN chief warns AI is outpacing regulation, urges global rules
stories.why_it_matters: The UN Secretary-General has publicly warned that AI technology is advancing far faster than governments can write rules to manage it, and is calling for a coordinated global regulatory framework. This is significant because fragmented rules across different countries create uncertainty for AI companies — which matters for holdings like GOOG, MSFT, and the GXAI.AX ETF. A global framework could either legitimise the industry further or add compliance costs.

stories.title: White House Adviser: Trump won't create an 'FDA for AI'
stories.why_it_matters: A senior Trump White House adviser has confirmed the administration won't create a dedicated AI regulator — essentially a 'food and drug administration for AI' — preferring a light-touch approach that lets tech companies self-govern. This is broadly good news for US tech giants like Google and Microsoft, which would face significant compliance burdens under heavy regulation. It reinforces the US as the more permissive environment for AI development compared to Europe.

stories.title: Spain pushes for AI regulation to protect workers
stories.why_it_matters: Spain is pushing the EU to beef up AI workplace protections — think rules around AI being used to manage, monitor, or replace workers. Europe is already ahead of most regions on AI rules via its AI Act, and Spain wants to go further on labour protections specifically. This creates a patchwork of rules that multinational tech companies operating in Europe — including Google and Microsoft — have to navigate.

stories.title: Model leaks: Mythos 1, Opus-4.8, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.5 Pro all reportedly in the works
stories.why_it_matters: Leaked information suggests major AI labs are racing to release next-generation models — including what appear to be GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.5 Pro, Anthropic's Opus-4.8, and a new model called Mythos 1. If even half of these land, it signals the AI model arms race is accelerating rapidly. For Google (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT), staying competitive in this race is existential — it directly drives cloud revenue and enterprise customers. Good context for why both stocks remain interesting long-term holds despite short-term wobbles.

sport.summary: Wimbledon is heating up with De Minaur into the second week, and the NRL is gearing up for Round 19 with some key injury and team news. AFL Coleman Medal race is tightening too.

stories.title: Alex De Minaur into Wimbledon second week — Australia's No.1 is a genuine contender
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's top-ranked tennis player Alex De Minaur has made it through to the second week at Wimbledon 2026. De Minaur has been one of the most consistent performers on tour and Wimbledon's grass suits his aggressive game. An Australian winning Wimbledon would be the biggest tennis story in years — worth keeping an eye on the draw as it opens up.

stories.title: Naomi Osaka eyeing Wimbledon title in stunning comeback
stories.why_it_matters: Naomi Osaka, once the world No.1 and a four-time Grand Slam champion, is in form at Wimbledon and being talked about as a genuine title contender. The SMH profile digs into her comeback journey — she stepped away from tennis amid mental health struggles and is now back playing some of her best grass-court tennis. A deep Wimbledon run would be one of the great comeback stories in sport.

stories.title: NRL tries to lure Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce as Knights end Dolphins' win streak
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL is reportedly making a Hail Mary attempt to attract Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce to an NRL game — presumably to replicate the NFL's massive ratings boost from their relationship. Meanwhile on the field, the Newcastle Knights ended the Dolphins' winning streak in a big result for Round 18. The Dolphins, who play in Round 19 at Kayo Stadium against the Sharks, will need to regroup quickly.

stories.title: Tigers skipper's injury fears calmed ahead of Round 19
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers coach and captain's injury fears heading into Round 19 have been calmed, with positive news emerging after Sunday's game against the Dragons. The Tigers face the Warriors on Friday night at Campbelltown Sports Stadium (8pm) — having a fit skipper is crucial for a team still fighting for finals relevance. The Dragons upset in Round 18 gives the Tigers some momentum going in.

stories.title: AFL Coleman Medal 2026: Charlie Curnow stalking Jeremy Cameron — King also in the mix
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's Coleman Medal (awarded to the competition's leading goalkicker) race is heating up in 2026. Charlie Curnow is closing in on Jeremy Cameron at the top of the leaderboard, with a third contender also in the mix. With the season entering its business end, the goalkicking race adds another layer of interest to every remaining round of footy.
